A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAE-V study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including v2's added Appendix C.3.

before.justification: V1 reports original SAE reconstruction and transfer experiments, ImageNet patch-filtering results, and multimodal alignment experiments with dataset and model comparisons.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds feature examples, model configurations, MMInstruct results, a small-subset study, and A-OKVQA masking results.

M1.justification: Equation 7 changes the reported feature-weight calculation from averaging rank-matched text-image cosine similarities to an expectation over independently indexed token pairs. This modifies the scoring rule used by Algorithm 1, while retaining the SAE architecture, training objective, and three-stage filtering pipeline.

E1.justification: V2 adds MMInstruct to alignment-data evaluations and A-OKVQA to filtering evaluations. Appendix C.3 extends the patch-filtering investigation from ImageNet image classification to visual question answering with separate question-text and image masking. The earlier datasets and benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding reconstruction, ImageNet filtering, and alignment experiments retain their comparator sets, including SAE, random filtering, and IFD. Although IFD's citation changes, Figure 11 and its description retain the same reported comparison; no substantive comparator replacement is established.

E3.justification: V2 adds Vicuna-based 7B/13B configurations for SAE evaluation, 13B alignment experiments, and a filtering-ratio experiment using 1/20 of Align-Anything. Appendix C.3 separately masks 0%, 25%, 50%, and 75% of text or image information on A-OKVQA validation data. Existing training/test splits and listed optimization budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine cross-modal feature meaning through Doberman and symmetry examples (Figure 3), whether small subsets support filtering-ratio selection (Table 2), and sensitivity to text versus image masking (Table 7). These substantially extend the questions investigated beyond the retained reconstruction and image-patch analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 42 for SAE training and report point estimates and curves without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's additional results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results include MMInstruct performance of 61.2 at 60% data (Figure 8b), 13B performance of 116.7 at 40% data (Table 3), and small-subset results (Table 2). At 50% masking, Table 7 reports 66.5% text-masking versus 78.4% image-masking accuracy. Existing reconstruction bars also change between v1 Figure 3 and v2 Figure 4, without an explained corresponding protocol revision.

T1.justification: Equation 7 revises the mathematical definition of cross-modal aggregation. Sections 2.1–2.2 also correct dimensional inconsistencies in the encoder/dictionary expressions and replace feature-vector products with latent-coordinate activation tests, propagated through the appendix algorithms. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: interpretable and transferable multimodal SAE features, their relationship to alignment, and filtering that achieves over 110% performance using less than 50% of the data. Added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning concrete and abstract cross-modal concepts, transferability as evidence of feature quality, small-subset filtering-ratio selection, and greater image redundancy relative to text. The stated limitations concerning theoretical understanding, unexplored modalities, and inherited dataset biases remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2's first-page footnote reports released code and models with GitHub and Hugging Face links, whereas v1 only promises release. Appendix A.1 additionally reports approximately 21 hours per SAE training run on the already specified eight A800 GPUs. The hyperparameter tables otherwise retain their settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds SAE-transferability references, acknowledges Zhang et al. (2024)'s earlier SAE work on multimodal models, and adds dataset citations. IFD's cited source changes from 'From quantity to quality' to 'Superfiltering.' Many other reference changes are publication or bibliographic updates to retained works.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order remain intact. Changes include localized explanations, a dataset-size analysis paragraph, Appendix C.3, corrected cross-references, expanded affiliations, and an acknowledgement. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds a cross-modal activation montage and three result tables, expands and recolors the reconstruction chart, and enlarges Table 1. V1's separate Chameleon dataset plots are combined with the new MMInstruct plot into v2 Figure 8. These changes substantially reorganize the results displays; existing appendix image cases remain.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the empirical case through concrete cross-modal feature examples, broader model/data evaluations, and targeted subset-size and VQA masking analyses. Mathematical corrections and code/model access information also help. The gain is limited by reporting inconsistencies: Table 1's caption generalizes higher SAE-V activation despite the opposite Vicuna-7B result, and revisions to existing reconstruction bars remain unexplained.
